title: Chicken Caesar Salad with Griddled Chicken
changes_from_base: Same croutons, creamy anchovy dressing and romaine, topped with a griddled chicken breast per person cooked to 74 °C and sliced.
summary: This follows the classic Caesar method — the same croutons, creamy anchovy-mayonnaise dressing and romaine — topped with a griddled chicken breast per person, cooked to 74°C in the thickest part and sliced.
equipment: salad spinner or clean tea towels
ridged griddle pan or heavy frying pan

ingredients.item: skinless chicken breasts (about 150 g each), thick ends gently flattened to 2 cm
fine sea salt or table salt
ciabatta or day-old crusty white bread, cut into 2 cm cubes
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
fine sea salt or table salt
anchovy fillets in oil, drained, patted dry and mashed to a paste
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
romaine hearts (about 2), cut into 2 cm strips

steps.title: Bake the croutons
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Combine the bread cubes with the olive oil, grated garlic and a pinch of salt, scatter them across a baking tray and roast for 12-15 minutes, turning once partway through, until they're golden and properly crunchy right through to the middle — the croutons that give this Caesar its signature crunch. Cool on the tray so they keep their crunch.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the lemon juice, mashed anchovy, garlic and mustard powder together, then whisk in the mayonnaise, grated cheese, olive oil and pepper until smooth and pourable. Using mayonnaise rather than a raw egg yolk gives the dressing its classic creamy body while keeping it safe to eat. Taste and sharpen with more lemon juice if you like.

steps.title: Griddle the chicken
steps.text: Pat the chicken breasts dry, rub with the oil and season with the salt and pepper. Heat the griddle pan over medium-high heat until very hot, then cook the breasts for 5-7 minutes per side without moving them until they release easily and are well marked. Check with an instant-read thermometer that the thickest part of each breast reaches 74°C before resting for 5 minutes, which lets the juices redistribute through the meat rather than spilling out when sliced.

steps.title: Dry the leaves
steps.text: Rinse the romaine hearts, then blot them completely dry with a salad spinner or tea towel before slicing into 2cm ribbons ready for the bowl. Any clinging water would thin out the dressing and stop it coating the leaves properly.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.text: Toss the romaine with two-thirds of the dressing and the croutons, then divide between plates. Slice the rested chicken 1cm thick, lay it over each portion, spoon over the remaining dressing and finish with the cheese shavings and a grind of pepper. Serve at once while the chicken is still warm.

tips: Flatten the thicker end of each breast slightly so it cooks through evenly without the thinner end drying out.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before slicing so the juices settle rather than running out onto the board.
Dry the romaine thoroughly so the dressing coats it rather than sliding off.
safety: Check the thickest part of the chicken reaches 74°C with a thermometer before serving — judging doneness by colour alone is the common mistake to avoid here.
storage: Refrigerate any leftover cooked chicken within 2 hours and eat within 3 days, reheating until piping hot (74°C throughout) if serving warm. Keep the leaves, dressing and croutons stored separately and combine only when ready to eat.
